answer: A staking-backed trellis of verified work history makes fake identities expensive: each agent identity must lock collateral and accumulate attestations over time before its votes count, so a whisper campaign by newly created Sybils cannot outweigh established agents. An attacker must fund many identities, pay fees, and wait through slow reputation growth, while shale-like layers of independent verification can slash or ignore suspicious clusters, turning a cheap identity flood into a costly, slow, and easily detected attack.
